name: Wang Ji 王籍
dates: dates unknown; active under the Liang (early 6th century)
bio: Wang Ji (courtesy name Wenhai) came from Linyi in Langya. His dates are unknown; he was active under the Liang dynasty in the early sixth century. He was widely read and talented, and was admired by Ren Fang and Shen Yue.

Under the Tianjian reign he served as registrar to the Prince of Ancheng and held posts at Yuyao and Qiantang. Later he joined the staff of the Prince of Xiangdong and went with him to Kuaiji. He is remembered for one poem, "Entering the Ruoye Creek", whose couplet on cicadas and birds was long celebrated. (He is not the Tang poet Wang Ji 王績.)

poems.title: 入若耶溪 (Ru Ruoye xi)
poems.author: Wang Ji 王籍
poems.text:
艅艎何汎汎
空水共悠悠
隂霞生逺岫
陽景逐迴流
蟬噪林逾靜
鳥鳴山更幽
此地動歸念
長年悲倦遊
